title: Sample Reception, Unpacking and Barcoding
author: Leigh Jones
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfe5jjg6
materials: Tube Tracker is a software system to track the whereabouts of samples from the hospital site to the testing laboratory. Open up the internet browser (Google Chrome) and search for the designated tube track website.

Risk of exposure due to damaged or leaking materials! Without opening a sample pack bag, visually inspect the samples within it for gross leakage. If no leakage seen, proceed to next step. If leakage is observed Do not open the sample pack or remove any sample bags If a member of health and safety (H&S) is not already in attendance, contact health and safety immediately H&S will spray the sample bags with distel disinfectant Place the sample pack into a designated really usefull box labelled ‘leaked samples’ Place the lid on the really useful box Transfer the samples to the CL3 facility to disinfect and recover any remaining usable samples Usable samples will start at receipt stage again Unusable samples will be disposed of via autoclave process

Risk of exposure due to damaged or leaking materials! Visually inspect the individual sample bag for leakage . If no leakage seen, select case ' No Leakage '. If leakage is observed, select case ' Leakage '.
Pass the sample to a barcode lable operator.
Pass the sample to the barcode label operator.

steps.title: Log into the System
steps.instruction: Access the system using individual user credentials.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Logon' in the top right hand corner of the screen.
Enter the supplied username and designated password.
Click 'Sign In' once the relevant location is visible.

steps.title: Unpack and Receive Samples
steps.instruction: Unpack clinical samples from the medical carrier and register them in the system.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Unpack Box' icon from the main menu on the left hand side of the screen.
Scan the barcode label on the outer bag into the 'unpack box' field, ensuring the cursor is inside the field before scanning.
Scan the barcodes of each individual sample to unpack and receive them.
If a sample is scanned into the bag but not physically present, click the symbol next to the sample number to mark it as 'missing' and notify the sending site.
If a sample is physically present but not tracked into the bag, click 'Yes' when the system prompt appears to update the audit trail.

steps.title: Initial Sample Inspection
steps.instruction: The Sample Checker (SC) must visually inspect each sample for correctness and integrity.

substeps.instruction: Open the incoming samples box and a sample pack.
Remove one sample bag at a time.
Verify the sample is a clinical nasal or throat swab (incorrect samples include urine, faeces, or blood).
Check for a barcode label starting with a two-digit number followed by a letter (EDTA number).
Inspect the individual sample bag for leakage (liquid in internal bag).
Communicate the status (Correct, Incorrect, or Leaked) to the Barcode Operator.

steps.title: Process Correct Samples
steps.instruction: Register and label samples that pass inspection for further processing.

substeps.instruction: Barcode Operator: Scan the barcode through the sample bag twice: once on Barcode Reader 1 (Clarity software) and once on Barcode Reader 2 (to print 2 labels).
Barcode Operator: If scanning fails, check for an EDTA number on the pack; if still failing, 'force' the sample through for processing.
Barcode Label Operator: Advance the printer one label and cut with scissors.
Barcode Label Operator: Staple the unbarcoded label onto the sample bag above the zip lock (do not staple through the main compartment).
Sample Sorter: Verify that the printed barcodes match the original barcode in the sample bag.
Sample Sorter: Place correctly labeled samples in a 'really useful box'.
Fix the lid of the box once full for transport to the CL2/3 suite.

steps.title: Process Incorrect Samples
steps.instruction: Handle and document samples that are not nasal/throat swabs.

substeps.instruction: Barcode Operator: Scan the barcode through the sample bag twice (Reader 1 for Clarity, Reader 2 for labels). If unreadable, pass to Sample Sorter for manual paperwork input.
Barcode Label Operator: Advance the printer one label, cut with scissors, and staple the label above the zip lock.
Sample Sorter: Verify printed barcodes match the original barcode.
Sample Sorter: Record details on two 'Incorrect samples Covid19' forms, placing one printed barcode on each form (hand-write if barcode is incorrect).
Sample Sorter: Place labeled incorrect samples in a box labeled 'Return Samples' and fix the lid when full.
Place the sample into the box marked return/incorrect samples.
Rescan the barcode in the sample rejection application to register as rejected.

steps.title: Process Leaked Samples
steps.instruction: Handle and document samples showing signs of leakage.

substeps.instruction: Barcode Operator: Scan the barcode through the sample bag twice (Reader 1 for Clarity, Reader 2 for labels). If unreadable, pass to Sample Sorter for manual paperwork input.
Barcode Label Operator: Advance the printer one label, cut with scissors, and staple the label above the zip lock.
Sample Sorter: Verify printed barcodes match the original barcode.
Sample Sorter: Record details on two 'Incorrect samples Covid19' forms, placing one printed barcode on each form (hand-write if barcode is incorrect).
Sample Sorter: Place labeled leaked samples in a box labeled 'Leaked Samples' and fix the lid when full.
Place the sample into the box marked leaked samples.
Rescan the barcode in the sample rejection application to register as rejected.
